articles.title: Does the UFC Secretly Love Josh Hokit?
articles.description: Ask Uncle Chael is back, and this week's questions hit everything: marriage, folkstyle, a fight Chael says was stopped on a tap that never happened, and whether the UFC hates Josh Hokit. Jeff Finnegan leads off: should I have kids? Then CJS sets a wrestling round robin between Spencer Lee, Ono, and Roman Bravo-Young, and somebody has to go 0-2. Anthony asks whether to lock in on fitness and his own business first or find a wife at the same time, and Chael flips the order entirely: the wife is the one you want the most, and you do all of it at once. BOD asks why folkstyle is not popular on the world scene, and Chael explains why the American style no other country wrestles may be exactly why Americans run MMA. A fan asks about a fourth fight with Jeremy Horn, Eric Sands asks whether a man proving everyone wrong is living on his enemies' terms, and Chael tells the Florida story: Trevor Prangley, a submission stoppage he says he never tapped to, and a brutal locker-room interrogation by the commission. Plus why every great story needs a villain, why David Robert Web's geography numbers are fake news, and the Hokit question: Ciryl Gane got the promo video, Hokit got no mention, so does the UFC hate him? Chael's answer is a list of everything the UFC has handed him. The final question is a fan's top five UFC fighters of all time, and Chael wants the gold, silver, and bronze medals for himself. Uncle Chael does not do soft answers. Which question should he take next week? Drop it in the comments and watch more Ask Uncle Chael on the channel. 0:00 Ask Uncle Chael, Chael's favorite segment of the week 0:05 Jeff Finnegan asks: should I have kids? 0:20 Round robin: Spencer Lee, Ono, and RBY, who goes 0-2? 1:18 Anthony asks: fitness and business first, or find a wife too? 1:41 Chael's answer: wife first, and do them all at once 2:41 Why is folkstyle not popular on the world scene? 4:09 What is it like to be undefeated? 4:37 A fourth fight with Jeremy Horn? 5:23 Proving everyone wrong: living on their terms? 6:28 The Florida fight: "I did not tap" 8:19 Does every storyline need a villain? 9:50 David Robert Web's geography question: "your numbers aren't right" 10:57 Ciryl Gane got the promo, Hokit did not: does the UFC hate him? 11:56 US military or a life in AI? articles.title: Bruce Buffer Crossed a Line With Josh Hokit
articles.description: Bruce Buffer weighed in on Josh Hokit, and Chael Sonnen says it breaks the one rule production people are never supposed to break. To explain it, he tells the Arianny Celeste story, and the phone call that taught him how this business actually works. After the first Anderson Silva fight, Chael was told Arianny had said she was glad it happened to him, for all the trash he talked. He fired back. Then came the call: why did you go after her? She is off limits. There is a separation. Fighters on one side, production on the other, and the people paid to make fighters look good stay completely unbiased. The twist: Arianny never said it. She was innocent, and Chael clears her completely. The point stands anyway. Now Bruce. Chael puts it at a one out of ten, and thinks Buffer was actually trying to put Hokit over, then hedged with "I don't agree with everything he says" to keep his own hands clean, the same trap that ended Trent Lott. But look at the asymmetry. Hokit does not know when his next paycheck is, and two bad nights can end his career. Five years from now Bruce is still clearing seven figures, and if Bruce does not show up tonight, business does not change. If Josh does not, it does. And Hokit answered: this game licenses criminals and men fresh out of prison, while he has a degree, All-American honors, a family, and a spotless record, and he is outworking Ciryl Gane at the media game. Why is the announcer the one bringing him down? The closing: Chael softens it. Bruce really did not say anything that bad, it just was not nice and was not meant to elevate Hokit; it looked like Buffer wanted to disassociate himself. And if you want to be in the cage fighting business without getting your hands dirty, who exactly do you disassociate with? Chael remembers when people tried to disassociate from Joe Rogan: it disgusted him, he has not forgiven any of them, and he would not trust or do business with a single one, because they showed him who they are. His prediction: you will never hear about this again, it goes away. But Hokit is not a good guy to come after. If you come after him, you are going to take a bump, and when you do, you need to know you had it coming. 0:00 The Arianny story Chael has to tell first 0:51 The call: she's off limits, there's a separation 1:35 The twist, she never said it 2:25 Production makes fighters look good, and stays unbiased 3:04 Now we have Bruce Buffer and Josh Hokit 3:38 A one out of ten, but it still happened 4:23 Buffer tried to put him over, then covered himself 4:37 The Trent Lott lesson: association gets your hands dirty 6:30 Josh doesn't know when his next paycheck is 6:50 Bruce will clear seven figures either way 7:34 Hokit answers: criminals get licenses in this game 8:05 A degree, an All-American, and never in trouble 8:53 Bruce really didn't say anything that bad 9:09 If you don't want dirty hands, who do you disassociate with? 9:22 The Rogan lesson: Chael remembers who walked away 9:54 Prediction: you'll never hear about it again #UFC #MMA #JoshHokit

articles.title: Paddy's Looking in the Wrong Direction
articles.description: Paddy Pimblett is obsessed with Ilia Topuria, and Chael Sonnen thinks he is staring at the wrong fight. Chael starts with a simple question: what does Paddy have to do to become a BMF? Charles Oliveira and Diego Lopes live in that world, and Paddy is not there yet. Paddy started the feud with Topuria, he does not forget, and he is still not over Arman Tsarukyan. Ilia vs Paddy might genuinely be the biggest fight the industry can make right now, but Chael argues Paddy is locked onto one tree and missing the forest. So Chael plays matchmaker. His first pick for Paddy is Max Holloway: no good guy, no bad guy, closer in age than you think, and a prediction that flips depending on whether it is three rounds or five. His second pick is Charles Oliveira, the personal-feud fight. Then the title picture comes apart. Charles believes a win over Lopes earns him a title shot, and Chael pushes back on his complaint about Justin Gaethje getting them: Charles, you are the champion right now. Gaethje, meanwhile, is down to two options, retire or one more, probably against Arman. And underneath all of it sits the problem nobody wants to say out loud: Paddy, Max, and Charles all have a claim, but nobody gets to the belt without going through Tsarukyan first. 0:00 What does Paddy have to do to be a BMF? 1:13 Paddy is looking in the wrong direction 1:42 Ilia vs Paddy is the biggest fight to make 2:41 Chael's first pick: Paddy vs Max Holloway 3:16 Second pick: Paddy vs Charles Oliveira 4:27 Charles, you're the champion right now 5:34 Gaethje: retire, or one more vs Arman 6:21 Nobody gets there without going through Tsarukyan 7:59 The grudges are holding Paddy back #UFC #MMA #PaddyPimblett

articles.title: Cejudo Called Pereira Spoiled. Is He Right?
articles.description: Henry Cejudo says Alex Pereira is spoiled with opportunities, and that he needs to go win two or three more fights before he talks about another title. Chael Sonnen walks the whole career back and asks a simple question: what kind of favor is that? Chael remembers the first time he saw Pereira. Second UFC fight, jerking the curtain at Madison Square Garden in front of almost nobody, doing the bow and arrow, a 36-year-old kickboxer everybody said would fail. He got in the door on his history with Israel Adesanya, then fought on undercards for ten and ten, five different times, in fights even his fans never watched. To even reach Adesanya he had to beat Sean Strickland in a non-main event. He lost four rounds of the title fight, heard his own corner on a hot mic, stayed calm, walked Adesanya down and finished him. Then he gave the rematch away and lost the belt, which turned out to be the gift: freedom from killing himself to make 185. At 38, his light heavyweight debut was Jan Blachowicz, a former champion, won by split decision. His reward for always saying yes was more asks: a short-notice Prochazka rematch, then Salt Lake City against the number eight guy, hurt and sick, telling nobody. He moved to heavyweight for Jon Jones and got a monster kickboxer instead. Now he is 40, in a division he has yet to win, chasing the man who beat him. Spoiled? That is the hardest road in the sport. 0:00 Cejudo's hot take: you're spoiled with opportunities 0:21 Is he right? History argues the opposite 0:36 The curtain jerker at Madison Square Garden 1:31 The Adesanya history is the only reason he got in 1:54 Five undercard fights nobody watched 2:48 He had to beat Strickland just to reach Izzy 3:02 Down four rounds to Izzy, then the walk-down finish 3:39 Losing the rematch freed him from 185 4:01 Age 38: Blachowicz in his light heavyweight debut 4:53 Saying yes only gets you asked more 5:33 Salt Lake, hurt and sick, against the number eight guy 6:07 Heavyweight was about Jon Jones 6:53 Now he's 40, chasing the man who beat him #UFC #MMA #AlexPereira

articles.title: Ilia Topuria Hasn't Said a Word...
articles.description: Ilia Topuria has not said a word, and Chael Sonnen says that silence might be the smartest marketing move in MMA right now. Chael starts with Brock Lesnar, the one monster Vince McMahon would not let speak, because monsters do not talk. Paul Heyman did the talking for him. From there, Chael explains why marketing is never a guarantee, it is an experiment, and sometimes the accident wins. Nick Diaz no-showing the Georges St-Pierre press conference left an empty chair that Dana White thought had ruined the event. It became one of the most successful press conferences of all time. Topuria is running the same play right now, whether he knows it or not. He might be the hottest name at 155 pounds, maybe in all of MMA, and he can pick his opponent and his date. Paddy Pimblett is chasing him and playing it perfectly, but Chael explains why Topuria gains nothing by answering. The fight is huge either way. Then Chael asks the question nobody in the community has suggested out loud: what if Topuria is thinking about retiring? The money, the two-division world titles, the short career, it is all there. And saying it out loud might be exactly the prod that gets him talking. Watch to the end, then tell us in the comments: is the silence strategy, or is it an accident? Subscribe for Chael's take on the biggest stories in combat sports, every day. 0:00 Being quiet is seldom helpful in this business 0:43 Marketing is an experiment, nobody can guarantee it 1:22 Nick Diaz, the empty chair, and the accident that sold a fight 1:58 Topuria has said nothing, and it is working 2:34 The hottest name at 155 can pick his opponent and date 3:28 Paddy is chasing Topuria, and Topuria does not need to answer 4:28 The retirement question nobody is asking 5:17 Chael is inviting Topuria on to speak 5:51 Staying quiet makes us want to hear from him even more #UFC #MMA #IliaTopuria

articles.title: Paddy Called Dana vs Eddie the Dumbest Thing Ever
articles.description: The Dana White versus Eddie Hearn feud rolls on, and Chael Sonnen closes it out with the two questions nobody else is asking: what is Fury versus Joshua actually worth, and what does Eddie get if he wins? Chael's first answer will annoy people. Fury versus AJ is not as big as they are pretending it is. It will do a very good night of business if it is the only show in town, but for years Chael has said these two are fighting for nothing: no title, no contendership, no ranking, two men in seemingly their final fight out for one last cash grab. Now he has been corrected, because they have produced a world title, and Chael tells the full Mayweather versus Conor McGregor money belt story to show what a produced title is worth, including the lost billion-dollar belt he personally had to guard until security came for it. His question is simple: did Oleksandr Usyk hand them one of his belts? Then the feud itself. If Eddie wins, he does not leave a bigger promoter than Dana in power, connections, networks, distribution, or events, so Paddy Pimblett has a point that it is silly. But Eddie has already threatened to pull AJ, and Dana has not played his card. The man who owns the building that night can have Eddie removed, and Chael wants Paddy asked again whether it is still ridiculous, or actually pretty fun. Then the results argument. Hokit fought on the White House lawn and is about to fight at Madison Square Garden for the undisputed championship, the fastest path to a title shot since Brock Lesnar, with sponsors remodeling his house for the cameras coming. Take every word he ever said away and ask if he is in the same spot. He is not. So if this is disrespect, Chael's verdict is that disrespect is a wonderful part of the sport, and in ten years Hokit will not be remembered as disrespectful. He will be copied, and remembered as innovative. articles.title: Does Sean Strickland Want to Fight?
articles.description: The Strickland story gets stranger, and Chael Sonnen is now ruling out his own best theories one by one. Somebody new always seems to show up in a fighter's life, somebody with a tie to Hollywood who promises to make them famous and tells them how underpaid they are. Chael's problem with that theory: not one single athlete, not one single time, ever got what that person promised. He tests the money theory against Tim Sylvia. Sylvia never thought he was underpaid until Brock Lesnar was brought in, made champion, and paid 20 times what Sylvia was getting, and that is what got him sideways with the UFC. Could a rumor about somebody else's money have done the same to Sean Strickland? Chael doubts it. Sean is one of the best paid guys in the sport, and neither his last opponent nor his next one makes more than he does. So what changed? Chael admits he does not know, but he senses Sean is not going to get his way, and he points to Dana White's own words: the UFC is dealing with this with Sean right now, and it has dealt with it consistently, with somebody, the whole time Dana has been there. Chael also explains why he does not need a Strickland vs Imavov rematch, why Imavov should get the title shot, and why Sean himself agrees. Then Chael tells the story of his own day of realization, on a hill at 6:45 on a Sunday morning at 36 years old, when everything changed and nobody had gotten to him at all. Subscribe for Chael's take on the biggest stories in combat sports, every day. 0:00 Dana on Strickland: sideways with two of 700 athletes 1:04 What changed with Sean? 1:48 Pricing yourself out is how you say you don't want to fight 2:40 Cejudo gave the belt back and lost the PPV points 3:57 Somebody got a hold of Tom Aspinall 5:47 Tim Sylvia got sideways over Brock Lesnar's pay 7:10 Dana: we've dealt with this consistently, with somebody 7:39 Imavov deserves the title shot, and Sean agrees 8:12 Chael's day of realization: 6:45 AM, age 36 #ChaelSonnen #UFC #SeanStrickland #DanaWhite #MMA

articles.title: Manel Kape CONFIRMS Joshua Van fight, soccer with Khabib, Kai Kara-France CALLOUT | Daniel Cormier
articles.description: Manel Kape joins Daniel Cormier for a BRAND-NEW EPISODE of the Daniel Cormier Show! Kape has been going back-and-forth with the UFC flyweight champion Joshua Van, as a title fight had seemed to be brewing between the two. Manel tells DC he's next for the title, and why he believes it could take place in January of 2027. Kape also talks about his soccer career, and about one time that Islam Makhachev told him to calm down because he was getting Khabib Nurmagomedov angry! And don't miss Kape decide to randomly go off on Kai Kara-France, a fighter who had previous beef with Manel in the division. Kape also gives his take on Van's victory over Alexandre Pantoja, and why he'll be able to "easily" take care of Van on his way to a title, despite also giving Van his flowers for his toughness. articles.title: STACKED Under The Radar Boxing Card This Saturday!
The Truth About Khamzat Chimaev’s 42-Pound Weight Cut #ufc
articles.description: Did Khamzat Chimaev really lose 42 pounds in a week to fight Sean Strickland? Chael Sonnen says the story is completely false. Chael challenges the reports about Khamzat’s supposed walking weight, arguing that he doesn't believe Chimaev has ever been as heavy as 220 pounds. He points to what he has observed instead: Khamzat appearing relatively small on weigh-in day, even when competing against welterweights. But the bigger question is whether Chimaev should move up to 205 pounds. Chael believes Khamzat could compete at light heavyweight, but says the decision needs to be carefully considered. If Khamzat moves up and becomes champion, Chael doesn't want to see him bouncing back and forth between divisions. Choosing 205 pounds means committing to the division, win or lose. So is Khamzat Chimaev really preparing to move up, or has the conversation about his size gotten ahead of the facts? #ChaelSonnen #KhamzatChimaev #SeanStrickland #UFC #MMA #LightHeavyweight #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis
